chunks: Abu'l Husayn Muhammad ibn Harun al-Zanjani informed us, he said: Mu'adh ibn al-Muthanna al-'Anbari narrated to us, he said: 'Abdullah ibn Asma' narrated to us, he said: Juwayriyya narrated to us from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Mansur, from Abu Wa'il, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said:

I found in some of the books of God, Mighty and Majestic: that Yusuf (peace be upon him) passed in his procession by the wife of al-'Aziz, and she was sitting on a garbage heap. She said: 'Praise be to God who made kings into slaves through their disobedience, and made slaves into kings through their obedience. Poverty has afflicted us, so give us charity.'

Yusuf (peace be upon him) said: 'Neglecting blessings is the ailment that ends their continuance. So return to what purifies you from the filth of sin, for indeed the place of divine acceptance is the sanctity of hearts and the purity of deeds.' She said: 'I have not yet clothed myself in the garment of penitence, and I am ashamed that God should see me in a position of supplication while the eye has not yet shed its tears and the body has not fulfilled its regret.'

Yusuf said to her: 'Then strive! For the path is the goal of possibility, before provisions run short and the allotted time expires.' She said: 'That is my belief, and you will hear of it if I outlive you.' So he ordered that a quintar of gold be given to her. She said: 'Sustenance alone suffices—I would not return to luxury while I am captive in divine wrath.'

One of Yusuf's sons said to Yusuf: 'O my father, who is this woman for whom my liver is shattered and my heart has become tender?' He said: 'This is a creature of sorrow in the ropes of retribution.' Then Yusuf (peace be upon him) married her, and found her to be a virgin. He said: 'How is this when you had a husband?!' She said: 'He was afflicted by the loss of movement and the coldness of the passages.'

key_terms.استعطاف: Seeking compassion or clemency — she is too ashamed to plead before God without genuine tears
key_terms.التأثم: Penitence, the state of abstaining from sin — she claims she has not yet fully adopted the outward form of repentance
key_terms.غموط: Neglecting, showing ingratitude for blessings — a rare classical Arabic word describing the attitude of taking divine gifts for granted
key_terms.فاقة: Severe poverty, destitution — indicating the complete reversal of Zulaikha's former wealth
key_terms.مزبلة: Garbage heap, dunghill — symbolizing her utter degradation from her former status

ai.seo_question: What happened when Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) met the wife of al-Aziz after she fell into poverty?
ai.summary: This narration, transmitted through Wahb ibn Munabbih from earlier scriptures (Isra'iliyyat), tells the dramatic encounter between Prophet Yusuf (Joseph, AS) after his rise to power in Egypt and the wife of al-'Aziz (traditionally identified as Zulaikha), who had fallen into abject poverty. The dialogue reveals profound moral insights: Zulaikha acknowledges that God reverses the fortunes of kings and slaves based on their obedience, while Yusuf counsels her that divine acceptance requires inner purity, not merely outward supplication. Her insistence on taking only bare sustenance rather than wealth demonstrates her genuine repentance, and the narrative culminates in their marriage.
